explanations.3: The double asterisks (**) mean 'match any number of folders deep', so this pattern finds all .sh files anywhere in the project.
explanations.5: This matches the hidden file .bash_aliases in any directory (the dot at the start makes it hidden on Unix systems).
explanations.12: These are shell options that make scripts fail loudly: nounset stops you using undefined variables, errexit exits immediately if any command fails, and pipefail catches failures even in the middle of a pipe chain.
explanations.14: Always wrap variable names in braces and quotes like "${var}" so that spaces or special characters inside the variable don't break your command.
explanations.15: Without quotes, a variable like $file gets split on spaces and whitespace, turning one filename into many, and glob patterns (like *) get expanded.
explanations.16: Use $(command) to run a command and capture its output because it's clearer; the old backtick style `` `command` `` is hard to read and nest.
explanations.17: Use [[ ]] instead of [ ] in bash because [[ ]] handles quoting edge cases better, and it's the modern standard.
explanations.19: If you write result=$(cmd) || echo "Error", the error message prints but the script keeps running—you have to explicitly return 1 or exit to actually fail.
explanations.21: That comment tells shellcheck (a bash linter) to ignore a warning—use it only when you have a good reason to check $? instead of running the command directly in an if.
explanations.23: If you use set -o pipefail and grep finds nothing, it exits with code 1 and kills your script; add || true to say 'it's okay if this command fails'.
